CAT.rationale: Caterpillar's fundamental health is genuinely strong — Q1 2026 revenue +22.2% YoY, EPS +30.2% YoY, OCF +45.1% YoY, and a durable franchise with 16-20% global market share and $24B in services revenue. However, the valuation has become severely disconnected from fundamentals. At 43.3x PE (vs. 20.1x a year ago), 21.9x P/B, and 5.8x P/S (vs. peer median 2.5x), the stock is priced for perfection on a cyclical industrial with 13.3% net margins. The earnings yield of 2.3% sits 227bps below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.57%, implying the market is paying a premium over risk-free for cyclical exposure. Net margin has compressed from 15.7% to 13.3%, Resource Industries profit plunged 39% YoY with 700bps margin compression, and balance-sheet leverage at 4.12x liabilities-to-equity magnifies downside risk. The PE has doubled in twelve months while EPS grew only 30% — the stock has re-rated as an 'AI-infrastructure proxy' via data center generators, a narrative that is fragile if hyperscaler capex decelerates. Michael Burry's short thesis at $1,060.98 (Jul 1, 2026) citing 30-year high P/S has structural merit. The stock has already corrected ~17% from its 52-week high of $1,073.46, but at $877 still trades at a level that embeds years of flawless execution at peak margins. Tariff headwinds of $2.2-2.4B and potential tariff refunds of $1.5-1.8B create binary outcome risk. The near-term catalyst of Q2 2026 earnings (consensus $6.25 EPS, +32% YoY) could disappoint given margin compression trends, making this a negative rerating risk rather than a positive one. All three pillars align bearish: deteriorating margin trajectory, extreme valuation vs. own history, and a credible near-term downside catalyst.
